equation_request.abstract: We report an experiment to demonstrate a quantum permutation determining algorithm with linear optical system. By employing photon polarization and spatial modes, we realize the quantum ququart states and all the essential permutation transformations. Compared with the classical case, this work determines the parity of the permutation in only one step of evaluation and displays the remarkable speedup of quantum algorithm. This experiment is accomplished in single photon level and exhibits strong universality in quantum computation.

specification.problem: Given a black box U_sigma|x>=|sigma(x)> for a permutation sigma of {0,1,2,3} on 2 qubits, output the parity (even/odd) of sigma using one query. Reconstructed as a 3-qubit Hadamard test with a fixed ququart probe state |phi>, then a classical lookup/threshold on P(0).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: 4-element permutations, a single controlled-U_sigma query, 3 qubits. The probe |phi> is a fixed state with phases found by an offline classical search over the 24 permutations. Out of scope: the photonic polarization x path implementation, the experimental fidelity analysis, the antisymmetric two-ququart variant, and any claim that this matches the paper's actual protocol.

symbols.meaning: fixed probe state on the ququart register, sum_x phi_x |x>
ququart integer, x = b_1*2 + b_0 with b_0 the least-significant qubit

equations.label: Parity as determinant
equations.description: The parity of a permutation equals the determinant of its permutation matrix, i.e. the product of its eigenvalues.
equations.justification: Standard fact; the abstract only says the algorithm determines the parity of the permutation.
assumptions: U_sigma is the permutation matrix on computational basis states

equations.label: Hadamard-test outcome
equations.description: Control in |+>, controlled-U_sigma on |phi>, H on control, then measure. P(0) is set by the real overlap.
equations.justification: Standard Hadamard test, used as a proposed single-query readout route. The abstract does not state it.
assumptions: Controlled-U_sigma is available as exactly one query
No extra phase is applied to the control

equations.label: Overlap in amplitudes
equations.description: The overlap computed classically from the probe amplitudes, used to tabulate expected P_0 for all 24 permutations.
equations.justification: Direct expansion of <phi|U|phi> for a permutation matrix.
assumptions: phi_x are the amplitudes of |phi> in the computational basis

equations.label: Separation requirement on the probe
equations.description: The probe must give disjoint overlap values for even and odd permutations. The decision then uses a lookup table or threshold: parity is even if c lies in the even set, odd otherwise.
equations.justification: Proposed design criterion. Existence of such a phi is not established here. A simple example phi_x=i^x/2 fails, because the even (01)(23) and the odd (02) both give c=0. A numerical search over generic complex phases is needed.
assumptions: A single phi exists that separates all 24 permutations
Otherwise use two probe states or a two-copy antisymmetric variant

equations.label: Decision rule
equations.description: Classical post-processing of the exact P_0 from the statevector: match c-hat to the precomputed sets, with tolerance ~1e-6.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_2 and eq_4. A pure threshold only works if the sets are separated by an interval; otherwise use the table.
assumptions: Table built with the same phi

registers.name: ctrl
registers.role: Hadamard-test control, qubit 0, measured into classical bit 0

registers.name: sys
registers.role: ququart register, qubits 1 and 2, with x = b_1*2 + b_0 (qubit 1 is least significant); holds |phi> and the black box target

steps.description: Prepare |phi> on sys from |00> with standard gates (Ry, CX, P/RZ), using the phases found by offline search.
Place one controlled-U_sigma placeholder (control ctrl, targets the 2 sys qubits). This is the only query.
Apply H to ctrl and measure it into classical bit 0 (counts key last character). Do not measure sys.
Classically compute c-hat = 2 P(0) - 1 and decide parity by comparison with the precomputed sets.

specification.measurement: Measure ctrl only, into classical bit 0. The decision uses P(0) from the counts, or from exact probabilities in the simulator.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Offline: enumerate the 24 permutations, compute c(sigma), and verify eq_4 for the chosen phi. Online: c-hat=2P0-1, then look up the parity.
assumptions: The 4-element permutation acts on the computational basis of 2 qubits
A controlled version of the black box is available at the cost of one query
A single probe phi separating even from odd by overlap exists and is found by classical search; this is unverified here
The qubit count is 3 (the 5-qubit two-copy variant is not specified)
The control and ququart ordering is as given in registers
missing_information: The paper's actual state-preparation and permutation encoding, and how it reads the parity in one step
An explicit phi with verified separation
Whether the paper uses a controlled oracle or an uncontrolled one
Details of the antisymmetric or two-copy variant
